lost_facts.assertion: test_r2::test_failure_behavior__bad_roles_and_a_bad_tokenizer_abort_the_batch_and_write_no_report -- "an aborted pass must not write a partial report: [0, 0, 0, [], 0] != [1, 1, 1, [1], 9]"
lost_facts.evidence: Shipped format_batch (transcript lines 2719/3369-3386, identical text both places): the FIRST statement of the method is `self.last_report = EncodingReport()`, unconditionally, before the loop runs. Only `ExampleTooLongError` is caught inside the loop; `InvalidRoleSequenceError`/`TokenizerCapabilityError` raised by `to_tinker_datum` propagate straight out of `format_batch`. Because the reset already happened before the loop started, an abort leaves `self.last_report` at the just-reset all-defaults value `EncodingReport()` == [0,0,0,[],0], instead of preserving whatever the previous successful batch had left. The oracle patch (fixtures/oracle.patch) instead accumulates into LOCAL variables through the loop and assigns `self.last_report = EncodingReport(...)` in ONE statement after the loop completes -- so a mid-loop exception never touches the attribute at all. The agent's version is the exact 'reset first, fill in later' bug the mail thread warns against. Neither carrier of this half of the fact was ever read: g9.r2.l19 (mail, 'Re: Weekly update: week of Apr 7', Dermot's review note on PR 632 -- 'when the batch aborted halfway, self.last_report had already been half updated -- it should still read whatever the last good run left') and g9.r2.say24/g9.r2.l17 (wiki comments on pages never fetched). The agent's own Analysis/Plan text never once mentions aborting, half-written reports, or preserving a prior report value -- see notable for the exhaustive search confirming this.

search_strategy: Mattermost: searched via /api/v4 .../posts/search with narrow term lists, then pulled full 200-post channel dumps for the 5 hit channels and grep'd those dumps with broad OR-patterns ('retained|16 |pair|ascii|dataclass|default|tuple|zero|drop|marker|bytes|supervis') -- this recovers most chat clues but produces many false-positive line matches (e.g. pointer-sheet line numbers for l16/l18 land on unrelated 'drop' chatter, not the actual remark) and can silently miss remarks whose wording doesn't share any of the OR terms. Wiki: two BookStack API searches ('encoding' -> 2 hits, 'finetuning' -> ~26 hits) followed by fetching only 6 of the ~15 comment-carrying pages by id (132,137,144,145,153,156); page 154 was RETURNED by the 'encoding' search but never opened (a clean 'found but not opened' near-miss), and at least 5 more pages (docs/engineering/end-of-run-summary-tables..., what-format-batch-counts-as-a-drop..., request-builder-what-we-drop-and-what-we-raise-on, viewer-dataset-download-export-format-notes-pr-652 partially, and two weekly meeting-notes pages) were never returned by either title search and so never fetched at all -- BookStack comments are unindexed by search so a page not found by title is invisible regardless of what's in its comments. Mail: dumped the admin mailbox to /tmp/mail.txt (231 lines) but only read lines 131-197 via two sed calls, leaving lines 1-130 and 198-231 (including the entire body of the Apr-7 'Weekly update' thread carrying g9.r2.l19) unread; a second IMAP fetch (/tmp/extra-mail.txt, 123 lines) searched only for literal 'Fireworks' or 'EncodingReport' in the body, which does not match several other relevant threads (l13's dataset-card mail, l-scope-1/l-scope-4/say23's PR-653 mail, h-role-row/rev3's mail). No truncation crashes or dead helper scripts; the misses are pure search-recall gaps, not tooling failures.
end_reason: Run completed normally: code was committed and pushed to Gitea main, CI presumably ran (provenance.pushed=1, provenance.ci_green=1, provenance.deployed=1), and the local finetune suite passed 120/120 before the push (line 3402-3411). g9.r2.failure_behavior scored 0 not because anything crashed but because one implementation detail (self.last_report must be preserved, not reset, across an aborted format_batch call) was never carried to the agent by anything it read.
notable: The reset-before-loop bug is visible verbatim in the transcript twice: line 2719 (`self.last_report = EncodingReport()` then the loop, then a single final reassignment at line 2734) and again in the final committed diff at lines 3369-3386. This is the exact shape of bug Dermot's unread mail (g9.r2.l19) warns about almost word for word ('the counters having grown outward from a local variable that was already there').
